Keywords: hover, press, button, link, card lift, feedback, cursor
Trigger: Pointer hover on a fine pointer, keyboard focus, and press
Do: Change colour or lift by 1 to 2 px; give :active a 1 px push; show the same state on :focus-visible.
Don't: Don't resize the element or move neighbours, and don't animate on touch screens where hover sticks.
Performance Notes: Only transform, opacity and colour change; wrap in @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine).
Reduced Motion: Keep colour and underline changes; drop the lift and scale.

Keywords: hover, image zoom, arrow nudge, card, thumbnail, link arrow
Trigger: Hover or focus on a card or media tile
Duration: 200 to 600 ms for media, 150 ms for small parts
Do: Zoom a photo to 1.02 to 1.03 inside an overflow-hidden frame and nudge an arrow 3 px.
Don't: Don't zoom past about 1.05 or let the frame jump in size.
Performance Notes: Scale on a composited layer inside a clipped box; avoid animating filter on large images.
Reduced Motion: Remove scale and arrow travel; keep a border or colour change.

Keywords: magnetic button, cursor follower, tilt, 3d card, spotlight, pointer tracking
Trigger: Pointer move over a feature element
Duration: Tracks the pointer; settle in 300 ms
Do: Use for one hero element at most, ease towards the pointer with a damped follower and clamp the range to a few pixels.
Don't: Don't tilt body text, cover content with a spotlight or attach it to every card.
Performance Notes: One pointermove listener, work in requestAnimationFrame, write transform only; disable on touch.
Reduced Motion: Switch the effect off completely and keep a plain focus ring.

Keywords: reveal, fade up, scroll, enter viewport, IntersectionObserver, section
Do: Fade and rise about 12 px once, using IntersectionObserver, and keep the end state in CSS so no-script visitors see it.
Don't: Don't hide content until script runs, and don't replay on every scroll back.
Performance Notes: Observe once and unobserve; animate opacity and transform; never read layout in a scroll listener.
Reduced Motion: Show content at once, with no travel; an opacity-only fade of 150 ms is fine.

Keywords: scroll progress, sticky section, pinned, scroll-driven animation, view timeline
Do: Map progress to one or two properties with CSS scroll-driven animations or a scroll library, and keep text readable at every point.
Don't: Don't pin a section for several screens of scroll with nothing new to learn.
Performance Notes: Prefer animation-timeline over scroll listeners; keep pinned height modest; test on a mid-range phone.
Reduced Motion: Remove scroll-linked movement; show the final layout statically.

Keywords: mask reveal, clip-path wipe, text reveal, cinematic, headline, scene
Trigger: Large heading or image enters view
Do: Reveal one dealt moment per section with clip-path or a mask and always keep the words in the DOM.
Don't: Don't split every heading into letters or reveal body copy.
Performance Notes: clip-path and transform are cheap; avoid animating blur radius on big areas; limit to the first view of the scene.
Reduced Motion: Show the finished heading and image, or a 200 ms fade.

Keywords: stagger, list, cards, grid, sequence, delay between items
Duration: 30 to 50 ms between items, 250 ms each
Do: Delay each item by a small step so the group reads as one wave, and cap the total near 400 ms.
Don't: Don't stagger more than about ten items or by more than 80 ms.
Performance Notes: Set delays with a CSS custom property per item; keep to transform and opacity.
Reduced Motion: Remove delays; appear together or fade without travel.

Keywords: menu items, nav links, tabs, dropdown, sequence, entrance
Duration: 40 to 60 ms between items, 200 ms each
Do: Slide items 6 px into place after the container opens, and close without stagger.
Don't: Don't make people wait for the last item before they can click the first.
Performance Notes: Items are focusable at once; delays only decorate.
Reduced Motion: Open the whole panel with a short fade.

Keywords: choreography, hero sequence, intro, timeline, orchestrated, entrance
Do: Plan one sequence with a clear order: background, headline, support, call to action; fire it once per visit.
Don't: Don't delay the call to action or block interaction during the intro.
Performance Notes: Run on transform and opacity; the timeline can be one CSS animation per element with delays.
Reduced Motion: Skip the sequence and render the final state.

Keywords: crossfade, route change, view transition, page, navigation, fade
Do: Crossfade only the changed region and keep header and footer fixed; use the View Transitions API where supported.
Don't: Don't fade the whole page to white or delay navigation for a transition.
Performance Notes: View transitions snapshot pages as images, so keep the pair small; fall back to an instant switch when unsupported.
Reduced Motion: Switch instantly or fade for 100 ms.

Keywords: shared element, morph, slide, list to detail, view transitions
Do: Name the shared element with view-transition-name so it travels from list to detail.
Don't: Don't morph elements whose content changes shape wildly.
Performance Notes: Give each shared element a unique name; the browser animates transform and size of snapshots.
Reduced Motion: Cut straight to the detail page with no morph.

Keywords: wipe, curtain, full screen transition, cinematic, loader between pages
Do: Use a masked wipe rarely, for a story-led site, and keep it interruptible by the back button.
Don't: Don't use curtains on a utility site or on every link.
Performance Notes: Mask with clip-path; keep layers under a few and avoid video behind them.
Reduced Motion: Replace with a quick fade.

Keywords: parallax, depth, background shift, scroll speed, layers
Trigger: Scroll through a hero or banner
Duration: Tied to scroll, 5 to 10 percent speed difference
Do: Move one background layer slightly slower than the page and keep text static.
Don't: Don't move text or large photos at different speeds.
Performance Notes: Use transform: translate3d on one layer; no scroll-event layout reads.
Reduced Motion: Static image; no speed difference.

Keywords: multi layer parallax, depth scene, storytelling, layered illustration
Do: Limit to three layers in one scene and test at 375 px width.
Don't: Don't stack parallax with pinned sections and reveals in the same view.
Performance Notes: Costly on phones; reduce layer count or disable below a width; keep images compressed.
Reduced Motion: Remove all parallax; layers sit in their rest position.

Keywords: skeleton, shimmer, placeholder, loading, content shape, spinner
Do: Shape placeholders like the final content and show them only after a short delay to avoid flicker.
Don't: Don't use a spinner for tiny waits or shimmer across the full screen.
Performance Notes: Shimmer on a gradient with background-position is cheap if small; consider a static grey block.
Reduced Motion: Use static placeholders with no shimmer.

Keywords: progress bar, determinate, upload, spinner, step progress, loading state
Do: Show true progress when you know it, and the finished state with a short settle.
Don't: Don't fake progress that jumps to 90 percent and sticks.
Performance Notes: Animate transform: scaleX on a bar, not width.
Reduced Motion: Update the bar without easing; keep text percentage.

Keywords: carousel, slider, autoplay, rotate, slide, testimonials
Duration: 400 to 600 ms slide; dwell 6 seconds or more
Do: Start paused or provide a visible pause, keep controls keyboard-operable and stop on hover and focus.
Don't: Don't auto-rotate important content or autoplay with no stop control.
Performance Notes: Use scroll-snap and transform; offscreen slides should not load heavy media early.
Reduced Motion: Do not autoplay; switch slides instantly on user action.

Keywords: ambient, background drift, floating, slow loop, gradient shift, decoration
Do: Move one soft shape very slowly, keep it behind content and pause when the tab is hidden.
Don't: Don't add more than one loop per view or let it pass behind text.
Performance Notes: Compositor-only transform; use will-change sparingly and remove it after.
Reduced Motion: Stop at the first frame.

Keywords: pulse, breathing, marquee, ticker, live indicator, status dot
Do: Use for one live signal, such as a recording dot, and give long marquees a pause control.
Don't: Don't pulse call-to-action buttons forever.
Performance Notes: Animate opacity or transform only; stop when off-screen using IntersectionObserver.
Reduced Motion: Show a static dot and a text label; stop the marquee.

Keywords: particles, canvas, webgl, shader, animated background, generative
Do: Keep a canvas small, cap the frame rate, and stop it when not visible and on low power.
Don't: Don't run a full-screen shader behind text on content sites.
Performance Notes: GPU and battery heavy; measure on a mid-range phone and pause on visibilitychange.
Reduced Motion: Do not start it; show a still frame.

Keywords: active state, tap, button press, scale, haptic feel, ripple
Do: Scale to .985 and push 1 px so the control feels pressed; return in 120 ms.
Don't: Don't start a press animation with a delay before it appears.
Performance Notes: Transform only; no layout.
Reduced Motion: Keep the colour change; drop the scale.

Keywords: modal, dialog, popover, drawer, sheet, menu, tooltip, origin
Trigger: Open or close of an overlay
Duration: 150 to 250 ms; sheet up to 500 ms
Do: Scale from the trigger's origin or slide a sheet from its edge; leave faster than enter.
Don't: Don't grow a modal from nothing or animate from the centre for a popover tied to a button.
Performance Notes: Opacity and transform; avoid animating box-shadow or height.
Reduced Motion: Fade only, 120 ms.

Keywords: count up, odometer, number, statistic, tabular nums, metric
Do: Count once on the first view, use tabular numerals so width stays still, and write the final value in the HTML.
Don't: Don't count on every scroll or animate prices and totals people must read at once.
Performance Notes: Update text in rAF; for many numbers use CSS counters or a single observer.
Reduced Motion: Show the final value at once.

Keywords: snappy, precise, crisp, productivity, tool, saas, fast, trading
Trigger: Every interaction on a tool, admin or finance product
Do: Use short ease-out moves, small slides, tight stagger and counters; keep the same curve and time family everywhere.
Don't: Don't add bounce, slow fades or large parallax.
Performance Notes: Almost everything stays on transform and opacity; fits low-end devices.
Reduced Motion: Keep colour and opacity feedback, remove slides.

Keywords: soft, floaty, gentle, calm, wellness, lifestyle, drifting, slow
Trigger: Every interaction on a calm brand or lifestyle site
Do: Use long gentle ease-in-out, slow fades, drifting layers and rounded shapes; the same pace for all elements.
Don't: Don't mix with snappy hovers or add quick flashes.
Performance Notes: Long durations are cheap but keep layers few; no blur animation on big areas.
Reduced Motion: Replace drift and parallax with a 200 ms fade.

Keywords: cinematic, bold, dramatic, editorial, launch, storytelling, big type
Trigger: Hero and story scenes on a brand-led site
Do: Use big type reveals, one pinned scene, full-bleed media and masked wipes, and give the call to action a clean path.
Don't: Don't use it on a service site where people want a phone number fast.
Performance Notes: Heaviest of the three; test on a mid-range phone and cap pinned scenes.
Reduced Motion: Show every scene statically in reading order.
